# Advanced Recipes

Complete, production-oriented AI applications built with langgraphr. Each recipe is a self-contained system you can adapt to your own use case.

---

## Recipe 1: Memory-Aware Chatbot

A chatbot that remembers conversation history, summarizes old messages when the context gets too long, and maintains a user profile.

```r
library(langgraphr)

chatbot_graph <- lg_graph("smart_chatbot",
  state = list(
    messages = list(type = "list", reducer = "append"),
    summary = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    user_profile = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    char_count = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite"),
    response = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

# Node 1: Check if we need to summarize
manage_memory_node <- function(state) {
  messages <- state$messages %||% list()
  total_chars <- sum(sapply(messages, function(m) nchar(m$content %||% "")))

  # If conversation is long, summarize old messages
  if (total_chars > 2000) {
    old_msgs <- messages[1:max(1, length(messages) - 4)]

    summary <- lg_call_model(list(
      list(role = "system", content = paste(
        "Summarize the conversation so far. Capture key facts about the user.",
        "Be concise. Include the user's name, preferences, and key topics discussed."
      )),
      list(role = "user", content = paste(sapply(old_msgs, function(m) {
        paste0(m$role, ": ", m$content)
      }), collapse = "\n"))
    ))

    # Keep only the last 4 messages plus the summary
    list(
      updates = list(
        summary = summary,
        messages = messages[(length(messages) - 3):length(messages)],
        char_count = total_chars
      ),
      goto = "update_profile"
    )
  } else {
    list(
      updates = list(char_count = total_chars),
      goto = "update_profile"
    )
  }
}

# Node 2: Extract user profile information
profile_node <- function(state) {
  last_user_msg <- NULL
  msgs <- state$messages
  for (i in seq(length(msgs), 1, by = -1)) {
    if (msgs[[i]]$role == "user") {
      last_user_msg <- msgs[[i]]$content
      break
    }
  }

  if (is.null(last_user_msg)) {
    return(list(goto = "respond"))
  }

  # Ask the LLM to extract user profile info
  profile_update <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Extract any new information about the user (name, preferences, goals, etc.).",
      "If no new info, respond with 'NONE'.",
      "Current profile:", state$user_profile %||% "No profile yet."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = last_user_msg)
  ), temperature = 0, max_tokens = 100)

  if (!grepl("NONE", profile_update, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    current <- state$user_profile %||% ""
    new_profile <- if (nchar(current) > 0) {
      paste(current, profile_update, sep = "\n")
    } else {
      profile_update
    }
    list(updates = list(user_profile = new_profile), goto = "respond")
  } else {
    list(goto = "respond")
  }
}

# Node 3: Generate response with full context
respond_node <- function(state) {
  # Build the system prompt with summary and profile
  sys_parts <- c("You are a helpful, friendly assistant.")

  if (!is.null(state$summary) && nchar(state$summary) > 0) {
    sys_parts <- c(sys_parts, paste("Previous conversation summary:", state$summary))
  }

  if (!is.null(state$user_profile) && nchar(state$user_profile) > 0) {
    sys_parts <- c(sys_parts, paste("User profile:", state$user_profile))
  }

  sys_prompt <- paste(sys_parts, collapse = "\n\n")

  # Build message list
  messages <- c(list(list(role = "system", content = sys_prompt)), state$messages)

  response <- lg_call_model(messages)

  list(
    updates = list(
      response = response,
      messages = list(role = "assistant", content = response)
    )
  )
}

chatbot <- chatbot_graph |>
  lg_add_node("manage_memory", manage_memory_node) |>
  lg_add_node("update_profile", profile_node) |>
  lg_add_node("respond", respond_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("manage_memory", "update_profile") |>
  lg_add_edge("update_profile", "respond") |>
  lg_compile()

# Usage in a loop
# graph$invoke("Hi, I'm Sarah and I'm learning R")
# graph$invoke("What data visualization packages do you recommend?")
# graph$invoke("What is my name?")  # The bot remembers
```

## Recipe 2: Data Analysis Agent

An agent that can load data, explore it, generate visualizations, and answer questions about the data.

```r
library(langgraphr)

agent <- lg_connect()

# Tool: Load and describe a CSV file
load_data <- function(filepath) {
  df <- read.csv(filepath)
  list(
    file = filepath,
    rows = nrow(df),
    cols = ncol(df),
    columns = names(df),
    head = head(df, 3),
    summary = summary(df)
  )
}
agent$add_tool(load_data,
  description = "Load a CSV file and return its structure, dimensions, and summary stats")

# Tool: Compute statistics
compute_stats <- function(data, column, stat = "all") {
  vals <- data[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    return(paste("Column", column, "is not numeric. Unique values:", paste(unique(vals), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  switch(stat,
    "mean"   = mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    "median" = median(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    "sd"     = sd(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    "min"    = min(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    "max"    = max(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    "all"    = list(mean = mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                    median = median(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                    sd = sd(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                    min = min(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                    max = max(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                    n_missing = sum(is.na(vals)))
  )
}
agent$add_tool(compute_stats,
  description = "Compute statistics for a column in a data frame. Options: mean, median, sd, min, max, all",
  parameters = list(
    type = "object",
    properties = list(
      data = list(type = "string", description = "JSON string of the data frame"),
      column = list(type = "string", description = "The column name to analyze"),
      stat = list(type = "string", description = "Which statistic to compute (default: all)")
    ),
    required = c("data", "column")
  ))

# Tool: Filter data
filter_data <- function(data, column, value) {
  data[data[[column]] == value, ]
}
agent$add_tool(filter_data,
  description = "Filter a data frame to rows where a column equals a value")

# Tool: Create a plot
create_plot <- function(data, x_col, y_col = NULL, plot_type = "scatter") {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  png(tmp, width = 800, height = 500)

  if (plot_type == "histogram") {
    hist(data[[x_col]], main = paste("Histogram of", x_col),
         xlab = x_col, col = "#5b5bd6", border = "white")
  } else if (plot_type == "bar") {
    barplot(table(data[[x_col]]), main = paste("Bar chart of", x_col),
            col = "#5b5bd6", border = "white")
  } else if (!is.null(y_col)) {
    plot(data[[x_col]], data[[y_col]], main = paste(y_col, "vs", x_col),
         xlab = x_col, ylab = y_col, pch = 19, col = "#5b5bd6")
  } else {
    plot(data[[x_col]], main = paste(x_col, "over rows"),
         ylab = x_col, type = "l", col = "#5b5bd6")
  }

  dev.off()
  paste("Plot saved to:", tmp)
}
agent$add_tool(create_plot,
  description = "Create a plot from data. Types: scatter, histogram, bar. For scatter, provide x_col and y_col.",
  parameters = list(
    type = "object",
    properties = list(
      data = list(type = "string", description = "JSON string of the data frame"),
      x_col = list(type = "string", description = "Column for x-axis"),
      y_col = list(type = "string", description = "Column for y-axis (optional)"),
      plot_type = list(type = "string", description = "scatter, histogram, or bar (default: scatter)")
    ),
    required = c("data", "x_col")
  ))

# Tool: Correlation analysis
correlations <- function(data) {
  nums <- data[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
  if (ncol(nums) < 2) return("Not enough numeric columns for correlation analysis.")

  cor_matrix <- cor(nums, use = "complete.obs")
  # Find strongest correlations
  cor_vals <- as.vector(cor_matrix[lower.tri(cor_matrix)])
  cor_order <- order(abs(cor_vals), decreasing = TRUE)

  pairs <- which(lower.tri(cor_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)
  pairs <- pairs[cor_order, ]

  top_pairs <- lapply(head(cor_order, 3), function(i) {
    list(
      col1 = names(nums)[pairs[i, 1]],
      col2 = names(nums)[pairs[i, 2]],
      correlation = round(cor_vals[i], 3)
    )
  })

  top_pairs
}
agent$add_tool(correlations,
  description = "Find the strongest correlations between numeric columns in a data frame")

# Example usage
sales_data <- data.frame(
  product = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  revenue = c(120, 340, 95, 210, 175),
  units = c(12, 45, 8, 28, 21),
  rating = c(4.2, 4.5, 3.1, 4.0, 3.8)
)

result <- agent$invoke(paste0(
  "Here is sales data: ", jsonlite::toJSON(sales_data, auto_unbox = TRUE),
  ". Analyze the data: compute summary stats for revenue,",
  " find correlations, and tell me which product has the highest revenue."
))
cat(result$content)
```

## Recipe 3: Code Assistant

An agent that can write, review, test, and explain R code.

```r
library(langgraphr)

agent <- lg_connect()

# Tool: Execute R code and return output
run_code <- function(code) {
  # Capture output safely
  result <- tryCatch({
    output <- capture.output(eval(parse(text = code)))
    paste(output, collapse = "\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    paste("Error:", e$message)
  }, warning = function(w) {
    paste("Warning:", conditionMessage(w))
  })

  result
}
agent$add_tool(run_code,
  description = "Execute R code and return the output. Use this to test code.",
  parameters = list(
    type = "object",
    properties = list(
      code = list(type = "string", description = "The R code to execute")
    ),
    required = c("code")
  ))

# Tool: Check if a package is installed
check_package <- function(package_name) {
  installed <- requireNamespace(package_name, quietly = TRUE)
  if (installed) {
    version <- as.character(packageVersion(package_name))
    paste(package_name, "is installed, version:", version)
  } else {
    paste(package_name, "is NOT installed. Install with: install.packages('", package_name, "')", sep = "")
  }
}
agent$add_tool(check_package,
  description = "Check if an R package is installed and get its version")

# Tool: Get function documentation
get_help <- function(function_name) {
  help_text <- tryCatch({
    rd <- utils:::.getHelpFile(utils::help(function_name))
    paste(sapply(rd, function(x) {
      if (is.character(x)) paste(x, collapse = " ")
      else ""
    }), collapse = "\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    paste("No documentation found for:", function_name)
  })

  substr(help_text, 1, 500)
}
agent$add_tool(get_help,
  description = "Get R function documentation and help text")

# Tool: Format code
format_code <- function(code) {
  # Simple formatting: consistent indentation
  lines <- strsplit(code, "\n")[[1]]
  indent <- 0
  formatted <- sapply(lines, function(line) {
    trimmed <- trimws(line)
    if (grepl("[}]\\s*$", trimmed)) indent <<- max(0, indent - 1)
    result <- paste0(paste(rep("  ", indent), collapse = ""), trimmed)
    if (grepl("[{]\\s*$", trimmed)) indent <<- indent + 1
    result
  })
  paste(formatted, collapse = "\n")
}
agent$add_tool(format_code,
  description = "Format R code with consistent indentation")

# Usage
result <- agent$invoke(paste(
  "Write an R function that takes a data frame and a column name,",
  "and returns a boxplot of that column. Test the code with the",
  "built-in mtcars dataset and mpg column."
))
cat(result$content)
```

## Recipe 4: Content Generation Pipeline

A multi-stage content generation system: research → outline → draft → edit → format.

```r
library(langgraphr)

content_pipeline <- lg_graph("content_pipeline",
  state = list(
    topic = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    research = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    outline = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    draft = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    edited = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    formatted = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    word_count = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

# Stage 1: Research
research_node <- function(state) {
  research <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "You are a researcher. Gather key facts, statistics, and insights about the topic.",
      "Be comprehensive but factual. Include data points where possible."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$input)
  ))
  list(updates = list(topic = state$input, research = research), goto = "outline")
}

# Stage 2: Create outline
outline_node <- function(state) {
  outline_text <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Create a detailed outline for an article based on the research.",
      "Format as: SECTION: Title | Description",
      "Include 4-6 sections."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0("Topic: ", state$topic, "\n\nResearch:\n", state$research))
  ))

  # Parse outline into structured list
  sections <- strsplit(outline_text, "\n")[[1]]
  sections <- trimws(sections)
  sections <- sections[nchar(sections) > 0]
  sections <- sub("^SECTION:\\s*", "", sections)

  list(updates = list(outline = sections), goto = "draft")
}

# Stage 3: Write draft
draft_node <- function(state) {
  draft <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Write a full article based on this outline and research.",
      "Target 500-800 words. Include an introduction and conclusion.",
      "Use the research for factual content and citations."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Topic: ", state$topic,
      "\n\nResearch:\n", state$research,
      "\n\nOutline:\n", paste(state$outline, collapse = "\n")
    ))
  ), max_tokens = 1000)

  words <- length(strsplit(draft, "\\s+")[[1]])

  list(updates = list(draft = draft, word_count = words), goto = "edit")
}

# Stage 4: Edit
edit_node <- function(state) {
  edited <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Edit this article for:",
      "1. Clarity and readability",
      "2. Grammar and spelling",
      "3. Flow between paragraphs",
      "4. Strong opening and closing",
      "5. Remove redundancy",
      "Return only the edited article."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$draft
  )), max_tokens = 1000)

  list(updates = list(edited = edited), goto = "format")
}

# Stage 5: Format
format_node <- function(state) {
  formatted <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Format this article for publication:",
      "- Add a compelling title",
      "- Use markdown headings (##)",
      "- Add bullet points where appropriate",
      "- Bold key terms",
      "Return only the formatted article."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$edited
  )), max_tokens = 1000)

  words <- length(strsplit(formatted, "\\s+")[[1]])

  list(updates = list(formatted = formatted, word_count = words))
}

pipeline <- content_pipeline |>
  lg_add_node("research", research_node) |>
  lg_add_node("outline", outline_node) |>
  lg_add_node("draft", draft_node) |>
  lg_add_node("edit", edit_node) |>
  lg_add_node("format", format_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("research", "outline") |>
  lg_add_edge("outline", "draft") |>
  lg_add_edge("draft", "edit") |>
  lg_add_edge("edit", "format") |>
  lg_compile()

result <- pipeline$invoke("The rise of R as a data science language")
cat(result$state$formatted)
cat("\n\nWord count:", result$state$word_count)
```

## Recipe 5: SQL Query Agent

An agent that translates natural language to SQL, executes it, and explains the results.

```r
library(langgraphr)

sql_agent <- lg_connect()

# Tool: Get database schema
get_schema <- function(table_name = NULL) {
  # In production, query the actual database
  schema <- list(
    customers = list(
      columns = list(
        id = "INTEGER PRIMARY KEY",
        name = "TEXT",
        email = "TEXT",
        signup_date = "DATE",
        tier = "TEXT (free, pro, enterprise)"
      )
    ),
    orders = list(
      columns = list(
        id = "INTEGER PRIMARY KEY",
        customer_id = "INTEGER (FK to customers.id)",
        product = "TEXT",
        amount = "REAL",
        order_date = "DATE",
        status = "TEXT (pending, shipped, delivered)"
      )
    )
  )

  if (!is.null(table_name) && table_name %in% names(schema)) {
    return(schema[[table_name]])
  }
  schema
}
sql_agent$add_tool(get_schema,
  description = "Get the database schema. Optionally specify a table name for details on one table.")

# Tool: Execute SQL query (mocked for safety)
run_query <- function(sql, max_rows = 100) {
  # In production, connect to a real database
  # For this example, return mock data
  if (grepl("SELECT.*FROM customers", sql, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    data.frame(
      id = 1:3,
      name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol"),
      email = c("alice@example.com", "bob@example.com", "carol@example.com"),
      tier = c("pro", "free", "enterprise")
    )
  } else if (grepl("SELECT.*FROM orders", sql, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    data.frame(
      id = 1:5,
      customer_id = c(1, 2, 1, 3, 2),
      product = c("Widget A", "Widget B", "Widget C", "Widget A", "Widget B"),
      amount = c(29.99, 49.99, 19.99, 29.99, 49.99),
      status = c("delivered", "shipped", "pending", "delivered", "delivered")
    )
  } else {
    data.frame(result = "Query executed. No matching mock data.")
  }
}
sql_agent$add_tool(run_query,
  description = "Execute a SQL SELECT query and return results as a data frame. Only SELECT queries allowed.",
  parameters = list(
    type = "object",
    properties = list(
      sql = list(type = "string", description = "A valid SQL SELECT query"),
      max_rows = list(type = "number", description = "Maximum rows to return (default 100)")
    ),
    required = c("sql")
  ))

# Tool: Explain query results
explain_results <- function(data, question) {
  explanation <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Analyze the query results and explain what they mean",
      "in relation to the user's question. Be concise."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Question: ", question,
      "\n\nResults:\n", jsonlite::toJSON(data, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
    ))
  ))
  explanation
}
sql_agent$add_tool(explain_results,
  description = "Explain query results in plain language. Provide the data and the original question.",
  parameters = list(
    type = "object",
    properties = list(
      data = list(type = "string", description = "JSON string of the query results"),
      question = list(type = "string", description = "The original user question")
    ),
    required = c("data", "question")
  ))

result <- sql_agent$invoke("What is the total revenue from each product?")
cat(result$content)
```

## Recipe 6: Document Summarizer with Hierarchy

Summarize long documents at multiple levels of detail: executive summary, section summaries, and key points.

```r
library(langgraphr)

summarizer <- lg_graph("hierarchical_summary",
  state = list(
    document = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    chunks = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    chunk_summaries = list(type = "list", reducer = "append"),
    section_summary = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    executive_summary = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    key_points = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    current_chunk = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

# Step 1: Chunk the document
chunk_node <- function(state) {
  text <- state$input
  # Split by paragraphs or every 1000 characters
  paragraphs <- strsplit(text, "\n\n")[[1]]
  if (length(paragraphs) <= 1) {
    # Split by length
    paragraphs <- chunk_text(text, chunk_size = 1000, overlap = 50)
  }

  # Merge short paragraphs
  chunks <- c()
  current <- ""
  for (p in paragraphs) {
    if (nchar(current) + nchar(p) > 1000 && nchar(current) > 0) {
      chunks <- c(chunks, current)
      current <- p
    } else {
      current <- paste(current, p, sep = "\n\n")
    }
  }
  if (nchar(current) > 0) chunks <- c(chunks, current)

  list(
    updates = list(document = text, chunks = chunks, current_chunk = 0),
    goto = "summarize_chunk"
  )
}

# Step 2: Summarize each chunk
summarize_chunk_node <- function(state) {
  idx <- (state$current_chunk %||% 0) + 1

  if (idx > length(state$chunks)) {
    return(list(goto = "create_section_summary"))
  }

  chunk <- state$chunks[idx]
  summary <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = "Summarize this section of a document in 2-3 sentences. Capture key facts."),
    list(role = "user", content = chunk)
  ), max_tokens = 150)

  list(
    updates = list(
      chunk_summaries = summary,
      current_chunk = idx
    ),
    goto = "summarize_chunk"  # loop for next chunk
  )
}

# Step 3: Combine chunk summaries into a section-level summary
section_summary_node <- function(state) {
  combined <- paste(state$chunk_summaries, collapse = "\n\n")

  summary <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Synthesize these section summaries into a coherent overview.",
      "Capture the main themes and conclusions. 3-5 sentences."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = combined
  )), max_tokens = 300)

  list(updates = list(section_summary = summary), goto = "executive")
}

# Step 4: Create executive summary
executive_node <- function(state) {
  exec <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Create a 1-2 sentence executive summary of the entire document."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$section_summary
  )), max_tokens = 100)

  list(updates = list(executive_summary = exec), goto = "key_points")
}

# Step 5: Extract key points
key_points_node <- function(state) {
  points <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Extract the 5 most important key points from this summary.",
      "Format as a numbered list, one point per line."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$section_summary
  )), max_tokens = 200)

  # Parse into a list
  point_list <- strsplit(points, "\n")[[1]]
  point_list <- trimws(point_list)
  point_list <- point_list[nchar(point_list) > 0]

  list(updates = list(key_points = point_list))
}

summarizer_graph <- summarizer |>
  lg_add_node("chunk", chunk_node) |>
  lg_add_node("summarize_chunk", summarize_chunk_node) |>
  lg_add_node("create_section_summary", section_summary_node) |>
  lg_add_node("executive", executive_node) |>
  lg_add_node("key_points", key_points_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("chunk", "summarize_chunk") |>
  lg_add_edge("summarize_chunk", "summarize_chunk") |>
  lg_compile()

# Usage with a long document
long_doc <- paste(rep(
  "R is a programming language and free software environment for statistical computing and graphics. It is supported by the R Foundation for Statistical Computing. R is widely used by statisticians and data miners for data analysis. ", 20
), collapse = "\n\n")

result <- summarizer_graph$invoke(long_doc)
cat("Executive Summary:", result$state$executive_summary, "\n\n")
cat("Section Summary:", result$state$section_summary, "\n\n")
cat("Key Points:\n")
cat(paste(result$state$key_points, collapse = "\n"))
```

## Recipe 7: Shiny Chatbot UI

A minimal Shiny app that wraps an langgraphr agent as an interactive chat.

```r
library(shiny)
library(langgraphr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("R AI Assistant"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      textInput("api_key", "API Key", value = Sys.getenv("LANGGRAPHR_API_KEY")),
      textInput("model", "Model", value = "deepseek-chat"),
      actionButton("connect", "Connect"),
      hr(),
      actionButton("clear", "Clear Chat"),
      width = 3
    ),
    mainPanel(
      wellPanel(
        style = "height: 400px; overflow-y: scroll;",
        uiOutput("chat_history")
      ),
      textInput("user_input", "", placeholder = "Type your message..."),
      actionButton("send", "Send")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  agent <- reactiveVal(NULL)
  history <- reactiveVal(list())

  observeEvent(input$connect, {
    Sys.setenv(
      LANGGRAPHR_API_KEY = input$api_key,
      LANGGRAPHR_MODEL = input$model
    )
    a <- lg_connect()
    agent(a)
    history(c(history(), list(role = "system",
                               content = "Connected! Ask me anything.")))
  })

  observeEvent(input$send, {
    req(agent())
    msg <- trimws(input$user_input)
    if (nchar(msg) == 0) return()

    # Add user message
    history(c(history(), list(role = "user", content = msg)))
    updateTextInput(session, "user_input", value = "")

    # Get response
    result <- agent()$invoke(msg)
    history(c(history(), list(role = "assistant", content = result$content)))
  })

  observeEvent(input$clear, {
    req(agent())
    agent()$reset()
    history(list())
  })

  output$chat_history <- renderUI({
    msgs <- history()
    html <- lapply(seq_along(msgs), function(i) {
      msg <- msgs[[i]]
      if (msg$role == "user") {
        div(style = "text-align: right; margin: 5px;",
            span(style = "background: #5b5bd6; color: white; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 10px;",
                 msg$content))
      } else {
        div(style = "text-align: left; margin: 5px;",
            span(style = "background: #e8e8e8; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 10px;",
                 msg$content))
      }
    })
    do.call(tagList, html)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Recipe 8: Email Assistant

An agent that drafts, reviews, and sends emails based on natural language instructions.

```r
library(langgraphr)

email_graph <- lg_graph("email_assistant",
  state = list(
    instruction = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    recipient_info = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    tone = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    draft = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    review = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    score = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite"),
    final_email = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    subject = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

# Step 1: Analyze the request and set parameters
analyze_node <- function(state) {
  analysis <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Analyze the email request and extract:",
      "1. Recipient info (who, relationship)",
      "2. Tone (formal, casual, urgent, apologetic, etc.)",
      "3. Key points to include",
      "Format: RECIPIENT: ... | TONE: ... | POINTS: ..."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$input)
  ), temperature = 0)

  # Parse
  tone <- if (grepl("TONE:\\s*(\\w+)", analysis)) {
    sub(".*TONE:\\s*(\\w+).*", "\\1", analysis)
  } else "professional"

  list(
    updates = list(
      instruction = state$input,
      recipient_info = analysis,
      tone = tolower(tone)
    ),
    goto = "draft"
  )
}

# Step 2: Draft the email
draft_node <- function(state) {
  email <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Write an email based on the instruction.",
      "Tone:", state$tone,
      "Include a subject line as: SUBJECT: <subject>",
      "Then write the email body."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste(
      "Instruction:", state$instruction,
      "\n\nAnalysis:", state$recipient_info
    ))
  ), max_tokens = 400)

  # Extract subject
  subject <- if (grepl("SUBJECT:\\s*(.+)", email)) {
    sub(".*SUBJECT:\\s*([^\n]+).*", "\\1", email)
  } else "No subject"

  body <- sub("SUBJECT:[^\\n]*\n?", "", email)

  list(
    updates = list(draft = body, subject = subject),
    goto = "review"
  )
}

# Step 3: Review and score
review_node <- function(state) {
  review <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Review this email for:",
      "1. Clarity 2. Tone appropriateness 3. Completeness 4. Professionalism",
      "Give a score 1-10. Format: SCORE: N | FEEDBACK: ..."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0("Subject: ", state$subject, "\n\n", state$draft)
  )), temperature = 0.2)

  score <- as.numeric(sub(".*SCORE:\\s*(\\d+).*", "\\1", review))
  if (is.na(score)) score <- 7

  list(
    updates = list(review = review, score = score),
    goto = if (score >= 8) "finalize" else "revise"
  )
}

# Step 4: Revise if needed
revise_node <- function(state) {
  revised <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Revise this email based on the review feedback.",
      "Address all issues raised. Return only the revised email body."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Original draft:\n", state$draft,
      "\n\nReview feedback:\n", state$review
    ))
  ), max_tokens = 400)

  list(updates = list(draft = revised), goto = "review")
}

# Step 5: Finalize
finalize_node <- function(state) {
  list(updates = list(final_email = state$draft))
}

email_agent <- email_graph |>
  lg_add_node("analyze", analyze_node) |>
  lg_add_node("draft", draft_node) |>
  lg_add_node("review", review_node) |>
  lg_add_node("revise", revise_node) |>
  lg_add_node("finalize", finalize_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("analyze", "draft") |>
  lg_add_edge("draft", "review") |>
  lg_add_edge("review", "revise") |>
  lg_add_edge("revise", "review") |>
  lg_compile()

result <- email_agent$invoke(
  "Write an email to my manager requesting 2 weeks of vacation next month. I have unused PTO."
)
cat("Subject:", result$state$subject, "\n\n")
cat(result$state$final_email)
cat("\n\nQuality score:", result$state$score)
```

## Helper Function: chunk_text

Several recipes above use this helper — include it in your scripts:

```r
chunk_text <- function(text, chunk_size = 500, overlap = 50) {
  n <- nchar(text)
  if (n <= chunk_size) return(text)

  chunks <- c()
  start <- 1
  while (start <= n) {
    end <- min(start + chunk_size - 1, n)
    chunks <- c(chunks, substr(text, start, end))
    start <- end - overlap + 1
  }
  chunks
}
```
